name: Pressable
tagline: Managed WordPress hosting from Automattic, priced by monthly visits
description: Pressable is a managed WordPress hosting provider owned by Automattic (the company behind WordPress.com and Jetpack), with plans priced by monthly visits and site count rather than shared-hosting-style storage tiers.
about: Pressable sells eight Signature plan tiers built entirely around WordPress rather than general-purpose shared hosting. Signature 1, the entry tier, includes 1 site, 30,000 monthly visits and 20GB of storage for $250/year ($20.83/month billed annually) or $25/month on monthly billing. Higher tiers scale both visit allowance and site count together — Signature 3 covers 5 sites and 75,000 visits, Signature 5 covers 20 sites and 400,000 visits, up to Signature 8 at 100 sites and 2 million visits. There's no cPanel here; management runs through Pressable's own custom dashboard, and every plan includes unlimited free WordPress site migrations.

Because plans are metered by visits and storage rather than sold as flat unlimited tiers, going over your plan's monthly visit or storage allowance triggers overage charges — Pressable bills roughly $1.20 per extra 1,000 visits and $1.00 per extra GB of storage. That makes it a poor fit for a site with unpredictable traffic spikes on a low tier; budget for the plan that comfortably covers your typical traffic rather than picking the cheapest one and hoping you stay under the cap.
policies: Pressable backs its hosting plans with a 30-day money-back guarantee.
